question: What percentage of tests will be positive for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in HHS Region 9 (the Southwest and Pacific) for the week ending September 19, 2026, in CDC data?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the percent of tests positive for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in HHS Region 9 (the Southwest and Pacific) for the week ending 2026-09-19 in CDC's the National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System (NREVSS) percent positivity data (data.cdc.gov dataset rgnm-fkqb), as posted on 2026-10-30.
research:
I pulled the CDC dataset and some news. Here are the findings.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on data.cdc.gov dataset rgnm-fkqb (NREVSS percent positivity), filtered to Region 9 and RSV, week ending 2026-09-19, as posted 2026-10-30. Each row gives tests, detections and percent positive. [dataset](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)
- **Caveat:** the API only serves the current version of the data, which can include revisions made after 2026-08-24. Below I report only weeks through 2026-08-15. That data would have been public by about 2026-08-21, since NREVSS updates weekly on Fridays. Small revisions are possible.
- Latest value usable for this exercise: **0.45%** for the week ending 2026-08-15 (14 positive out of 3,086 tests). [dataset](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The target week is about four weeks after the latest available data. Region 9 RSV is at its summer low, under 1%.
- Recent weekly values for Region 9 RSV percent positive (all from the [dataset](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)):
  - 2026-08-15: 0.45%
  - 2026-08-08: 0.76% (22 of 2,911)
  - 2026-08-01: 0.76% (22 of 2,887)
  - 2026-07-25: 0.51%
  - 2026-07-18: 0.85%
  - 2026-07-11: 1.55%
  - 2026-06-20: 2.24%
- The 2025-26 season ran late and long. It peaked at 7.58% in the week ending 2026-02-21, was still at 1.5-2.2% in June, and dropped to roughly 0.5-0.8% by late July and August. Summer 2026 started a bit higher than summer 2025 (0.4-0.6%), but has now come down to similar levels.
- With only about 14-25 positives a week out of about 3,000 tests, the weekly figure moves around by about ±0.2-0.3 percentage points from noise alone.

## 3. Recent news
- 2026-03 (approximate): CDPH extended its infant RSV antibody recommendation through April 2026 because the 2025-26 season started late and activity stayed high. [CDPH](https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/OPA/Pages/CAHAN/CDPH-Recommends-Immunizing-Infants-with-RSV-Monoclonal-Antibodies-through-April-2026.aspx)
- Late 2025: CDPH said RSV had started earlier than usual in the previous three seasons. [Patch](https://patch.com/california/across-ca/amp/31592780/8-dead-from-flu-and-rsv-in-ca-as-cold-and-flu-season-arrives-early)
- I found no news from August 2026 about RSV rising early in California, Arizona, Nevada or Hawaii. CDPH publishes a weekly dashboard (usually on Fridays) that would show it. [CDPH dashboard](https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CID/DCDC/Pages/RespiratoryVirusReport.aspx)

## 4. Base rates
Region 9 RSV percent positive in the same dataset, comparing the mid-August week to the week nearest September 19. All from the [dataset](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json).

| Year | Mid-August value | Late-August / early-September values | Value nearest Sep 19 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | 0.57% (Aug 16) | 0.39, 0.27, 0.45, 0.39% | 0.77% (Sep 20) | +0.20 pp |
| 2024 | 0.38% (Aug 17) | 0.49, 0.15, 0.33, 0.99% | 0.83% (Sep 21) | +0.45 pp |
| 2023 | 1.16% (Aug 19) | 1.35, 1.33, 1.88, 2.69% | 2.75% (Sep 23) | +1.6 pp |

- In 2023 the season started early. Testing volume was also smaller then, at about 3,000-3,600 tests a week.
- Pattern: mid-September usually marks the first small rise from the summer low. In 2024 and 2025 the target week came in around 0.8%. In 2023, an early-onset year, it was close to 2.7%.
- In both 2024 and 2025, early October brought a jump in test volume (from about 3,500 to 5,000-7,400 tests), which happens after the target week.
- Over four weeks at this time of year, the change has ranged from about +0.2 to +1.6 pp, and single weeks have swung by ±0.3-0.6 pp.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold markets, and no published expert forecasts, for Region 9 RSV positivity. CDC's RSV outlook and the respiratory forecast hubs focus on hospitalizations, not regional NREVSS positivity, and I found no 2026-27 outlook dated before 2026-08-24.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Weekly NREVSS updates (Fridays) will publish data for the weeks ending Aug 22 through Sep 19. The target-week value first appears around 2026-09-25 and can still be revised until the 2026-10-30 posting.
- Late August and September brings school reopening, which typically marks the start of RSV's seasonal rise.
- Infant nirsevimab/clesrovimab and maternal and older-adult RSV vaccination campaigns start in the fall. They mainly affect severe disease, so they will have limited effect on September positivity.
- The weekly CDPH dashboard and county reports (LA, San Diego) can give early signs of a rise.

Sources: [CDC NREVSS dataset rgnm-fkqb](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json), [CDPH Respiratory Virus Report](https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CID/DCDC/Pages/RespiratoryVirusReport.aspx), [CDPH CAHAN April 2026](https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/OPA/Pages/CAHAN/CDPH-Recommends-Immunizing-Infants-with-RSV-Monoclonal-Antibodies-through-April-2026.aspx), [Patch](https://patch.com/california/across-ca/amp/31592780/8-dead-from-flu-and-rsv-in-ca-as-cold-and-flu-season-arrives-early), [LA County Respiratory Watch](https://content.govdelivery.com/attachments/CALACOUNTY/2026/10/16/file_attachments/3820897/Respiratory%20Watch%20Los%20Angeles%202026-27%20Week%2040.pdf)
